datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 11
datasets.description: Release 11 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 430 participants aged 5-21 years performing three passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and three active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and participants.tsv includes quality-control results and psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 6
datasets.description: Release 6 of the HBN-EEG dataset, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network project, organized in BIDS format. It contains EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 134 participants aged 5-21 performing three passive tasks (resting state, surround suppression, movie watching) and three active tasks (contrast change detection, sequence learning, symbol search). Events carry HED annotations, and psychopathology factors derived from the CBCL (p-factor, attention, internalizing, externalizing) are provided alongside basic quality-control results.
datasets.authors: Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Face processing EEG dataset for EEGLAB
datasets.description: This dataset is the EEG and structural MRI portion of a multi-subject, multi-modal face processing study (originally ds000117), repackaged in EEGLAB format with augmented event logs and HED annotation. Eighteen participants viewed famous, unfamiliar, and scrambled faces while making symmetry judgments. The original study had two sessions (fMRI and simultaneous MEG/EEG); only the MEEG session's EEG data and the structural MRI are included here, while MEG and fMRI data are excluded. Minimal preprocessing, including EEG channel extraction, event correction, and resampling to 250 Hz, yields a lightweight version suitable for tutorials and EEG source localization.
datasets.authors: Daniel G. Wakeman, Richard N Henson

datasets.name: Multimodal EEG and fNIRS Biosignal Acquisition during Motor Imagery Tasks in Patients with Orthopedic Impairment
datasets.description: Raw multimodal recordings of 18-channel EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) from seven participants with orthopedic impairment performing motor imagery tasks. Each participant completed three sessions of 40 trials, with four motor imagery tasks (reach, twist, lift, grasp) presented in random order. The dataset supports research on multimodal brain-computer interfaces for people with motor impairments.
datasets.authors: Seho Lee, Hee Ra Jung, In-Nea Wang, Min-Kyung Jung, Hakseung Kim, Dong-Joo Kim

datasets.name: Healthy Brain Network (HBN) EEG - Release 1
datasets.description: Release 1 of HBN-EEG, the EEG component of the Child Mind Institute Healthy Brain Network (HBN) project, organized in BIDS format. It includes EEG recordings and behavioral responses from 136 participants aged 5-21 performing six passive and active tasks: resting state, surround suppression, movie watching, contrast change detection, sequence learning, and symbol search. Events carry HED annotations, and the participants file includes quality control results and CBCL-derived psychopathology factors.
datasets.authors: Shirazi, Seyed Yahya, Franco, Alexandre, Hoffmann, Maurício Scopel, Esper, Nathalia B., Truong, Dung, Delorme, Arnaud, Milham, Michael, Makeig, Scott, Seyed Yahya Shirazi, Alexandre Franco, Maurício Scopel Hoffmann, Nathalia B. Esper, Dung Truong, Arnaud Delorme, Michael Milham, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Gloups_MEG
datasets.description: This dataset contains magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from seventeen adult participants who completed a learning task and a resting-state condition. Data were acquired on a 4D NeuroImaging system with 248 magnetometer channels. The same participants performed an identical learning task during fMRI scanning, released as a companion dataset. The task involved the production of phonotactically legal and illegal pseudowords.
datasets.authors: Snezana Todorovic, Elin Runnqvist, Valerie Chanoine, Jean-Michel Badier

datasets.name: ArEEG: Arabic Inner Speech EEG dataset
datasets.description: ArEEG is an open-access inner speech EEG dataset recorded from 12 participants (7 male, 5 female) who were shown visual cues written in Modern Standard Arabic. It contains 186 continuous recordings from 8 scalp electrodes sampled at 250 Hz. The dataset supports research on inner speech decoding and brain-computer interfaces for Arabic.
datasets.authors: Donia Metwalli, Eslam Ahmed, Antony Emil, Yousef A. Radwan, Mariam Barakat, Anas Ahmed, Amro Omar, Sahar Selim

datasets.name: Assesment of the visual stimuli properties in P300 paradigm
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 19 participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface paradigm, designed to assess how visual stimulus properties affect evoked responses and classification accuracy. Each participant completed three sessions with varying numbers of stimuli (4 to 9) and two flash types, a standard flash and a superimposed cartoon face. Data were recorded from eight scalp electrodes (Fz, Cz, P3, Pz, P4, PO7, PO8, Oz) at 256 Hz, with markers encoding experimental phases and activated symbols.
datasets.authors: Omar Mendoza-Montoya, Javier M. Antelis

datasets.name: TDCS Modulation of Visual Cortex in Motor Imagery
datasets.description: EEG dataset investigating transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) modulation of visual cortex during motor imagery. Recordings were acquired with a Brain Products EEG system at 5000 Hz from a small group of healthy adult participants across three recording sessions. The dataset is organized in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Anthony Mensah, Gleb Perevoznyuk, Artyom Batov, Aleksandra S. Pleskovskaya

datasets.name: Dataset of Visual and Audiovisual Stimuli in Virtual Reality from the Edzna Archaeological Site
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings collected while participants viewed visual and audiovisual stimuli presented in virtual reality, depicting the Edzna Archaeological Site. It is intended to support research on neural responses to immersive, culturally relevant virtual environments. The data are organized in BIDS format with HED annotations.
datasets.authors: Juan Pablo Rosado-Aíza, Fernando José Domínguez-Morales, Tania Yareni Pech-Canul, Paola Guadalupe Vázquez-Rodríguez, Gustavo Navas-Reascos, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi, David I. Ibarra Zarate

datasets.name: Resting state EEG with closed eyes and open eyes in females from 60 to 80 years old
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings acquired from older adult females aged 60 to 80 years under two conditions: eyes closed and eyes open. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and is intended to support research on brain electrical activity in healthy aging.
datasets.authors: Miriam de Jesús Sánchez Gama, Luis Alberto Barradas Chacón, Leticia Chacón Gutiérrez, Thalía Fernández Harmony, Carlos Augusto Novo Olivas, José María De La Roca Chiapas

datasets.name: Comparing P300 Flashing paradigms in online typing with language models
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a P300 speller brain-computer interface study comparing flashing paradigms for online typing with language model support. The dataset was collected with BCI2000 to evaluate typing performance across different stimulus presentation schemes. It supports research on P300-based communication interfaces.
datasets.authors: Nand Chandravadia, Shrita Pendekanti, Dustin Roberts, Robert Tran, Saarang Panchavati, Corey Arnold, Nader Pouratian, William Speier

datasets.name: FT
datasets.description: A placeholder EEG dataset named FT, formatted according to BIDS with HED annotations. The README provides no further information about the experimental paradigm, participants, or recording setup. The dataset is a NEMAR-hosted copy of an OpenNeuro deposit.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: TX18
datasets.description: TX18 is an EEG dataset formatted according to BIDS with HED annotations, contributed by Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, and Kevin King. The README describes it only as a placeholder dataset, and gives no further detail on its content or purpose.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: TX17
datasets.description: TX17 is an EEG dataset formatted according to BIDS with HED annotations, contributed by Johnson, Gordon, Touryan, and King. The README describes it only as a placeholder, so no further details on the experimental paradigm or participants are provided. It is a NEMAR-hosted copy of an OpenNeuro deposit.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: InsurgentCivilian
datasets.description: InsurgentCivilian is an EEG dataset with HED (Hierarchical Event Descriptors) annotations, contributed by Johnson, Gordon, Touryan, and King. The README describes it only as a placeholder, so detailed information on the task, participants, and acquisition is not provided.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: ODE
datasets.description: ODE is a placeholder EEG dataset containing a single-subject recording of an n-back task with 64 scalp electrodes placed according to the 10-10 system. Event annotations use Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED), with 107 documented event codes. The record has been curated for BIDS compliance by correcting sidecar metadata, and the raw EEGLAB files are unchanged.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: STRONG
datasets.description: STRONG is a placeholder EEG dataset formatted according to BIDS with HED annotations. The README provides no detailed description of the participants, task, or experimental content. The dataset is mirrored from an OpenNeuro deposit.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: 8-Channel SSVEP EEG Dataset with Artifact Trials
datasets.description: An 8-channel wearable EEG dataset of steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) recorded from 6 participants. Stimulation was delivered at 2 Hz, 4 Hz and 8 Hz. Each participant completed trials while staying still and trials with voluntary head/neck and eye movements, so the recordings include both clean and artifact-contaminated data.
datasets.authors: Velu Prabhakar Kumaravel, Victor Kartsch, Simone Benatti, Giorgio Vallortigara, Elisabetta Farella, Marco Buiatti

datasets.name: ANDI
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 17 male participants performing a guided visual search task while simultaneously completing a binaurally presented auditory N-back task. The design includes a baseline condition in which the auditory stimuli were ignored, and dual-task conditions with N-back levels of 0, 1 and 2, which vary auditory working memory load. The dataset includes 64-channel BioSemi EEG with EOG and mastoid reference channels and is annotated with HED.
datasets.authors: Tony Johnson, Stephen Gordon, Jon Touryan, Kevin King

datasets.name: Neuma
datasets.description: Neuma is a multimodal neuromarketing dataset from 42 participants who browsed supermarket advertising brochures and selected the products they intended to buy. It combines EEG, eye tracking, questionnaire responses (demographic, profiling and product-related) and computer mouse data. The dataset supports research on consumer behavior and decision-making.
datasets.authors: Kostas Georgiadis, Fotis P. Kalaganis, Kyriakos Riskos, Eleytheria Matta, Vangelis P. Oikonomou, Yfantidou Ioanna, Dimitris Chantziaras, Kyriakos Pantouvakis, Spiros Nikolopoulos, Nikos A. Laskaris, Ioannis Kompatsiaris

datasets.name: Meta-rdk: Preprocessed EEG data
datasets.description: Preprocessed EEG recordings from 20 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder and 22 healthy control participants performing a visual random-dot motion discrimination task. Participants reported motion direction with a mouse and then rated their confidence on a visual analog scale. Motion coherence was individually adapted with a staircase procedure to match performance between groups, which allows metacognitive processes to be compared.
datasets.authors: Martin Rouy, Matthieu Roger, Dorian Goueytes, Michael Pereira, Paul Roux, Nathan Faivre

datasets.name: EEG recordings for 200 object images presented in RSVP sequences at 5Hz or 20Hz
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants viewing 200 object images presented in rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) streams at 5 Hz or 20 Hz. The dataset supports investigation of the temporal representational dynamics of visual object processing under rapid presentation conditions. It accompanies a published NeuroImage study on object representations in RSVP streams.
datasets.authors: Grootswagers, T., Robinson, A.K., Carlson, T.A.

datasets.name: Motor Imagery vs Rest - Low-Cost EEG System
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 BCI-naive participants acquired with a low-cost consumer-grade device during a motor imagery versus rest protocol. Participants performed kinesthetic imagination of a grasping movement with the dominant hand and rest/idle conditions across five runs, including an initial real-movement run. EMG of the dominant hand was recorded for protocol control, supporting evaluation of affordable brain-computer interface systems.
datasets.authors: Victoria Peterson, Catalina Maria Galvan, Hugo Sacha Hernadez, Ruben Spies

datasets.name: Neural Tracking to go
datasets.description: A mobile EEG dataset on auditory attention recorded from 20 participants. Using a two-competing-speaker paradigm, participants either sat on a chair or walked a route indoors while attending to one speaker. Attention was disrupted by salient environmental events presented from in front of the participant, allowing study of neural tracking of speech in realistic, mobile conditions.
datasets.authors: Lisa Straetmans, Bjoern Holtze, Stefan Debener, Manuela Jaeger, Bojana Mirkovic

datasets.name: Corticothalamic communication under analgesia, sedation and gradual ischemia: a multimodal model of controlled gradual cerebral ischemia in pig
datasets.description: A multimodal porcine dataset of corticothalamic communication recorded during analgesia, sedation, and controlled gradual cerebral ischemia followed by recovery. It includes 11 juvenile pigs monitored across sedation states (isoflurane, fentanyl, propofol), one or two ischemia episodes, and recovery phases. Animals were divided into a sedation-only group and an ischemia group.
datasets.authors: Martin G. Frasch, Bernd Walter, Chrstophe L. Herry, Reinhard Bauer

datasets.name: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG
datasets.description: EEG recordings from twenty healthy right-handed adults exposed to tendon vibration of the left elbow, designed to separate the percept of illusory movement from plain vibratory sensation. Sixteen sensorimotor electrodes were recorded while biceps and triceps tendons were vibrated at 90/50 Hz (illusion of elbow extension) or both at 70 Hz (control, no illusion). Each participant completed three blocks of 72 randomized three-second stimulations.
datasets.authors: Christoph Schneider, Renaud Marquis, Jane Johr, Marina Da Silva Lopes, Philippe Ryvlin, Andrea Serino, Marzia De Lucia, Karin Diserens

datasets.name: Placebo Neuroepo multisession
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recorded from patients with Parkinson's disease enrolled in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of Neuroepo, an erythropoietin formulation with low sialic acid content. Recordings were acquired before and six months after drug administration in Neuroepo (n=15) and placebo (n=10) groups. The dataset supports qualitative EEG abnormality ratings and quantitative source-level EEG analysis, and is shared as raw EEG in BIDS format.
datasets.authors: Maria Luisa Bringas Vega, Lilia Morales Chacon , Ivonne Pedroso Ibanez

datasets.name: Neuroepo multisession
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recorded from 25 patients with Parkinson's disease in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of Neuroepo, an EPO formulation with low sialic acid content. Recordings were acquired before and six months after drug administration, in Neuroepo (n=15) and placebo (n=10) groups. The raw data are shared in EEG-BIDS format to support evaluation of EEG biomarkers of neuroprotection, including qualitative expert ratings and quantitative source-level analysis.
datasets.authors: Maria Luisa Bringas Vega, Lilia Morales Chacon , Ivonne Pedroso Ibanez

datasets.name: UC San Diego Resting State EEG Data from Patients with Parkinson's Disease
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recorded at UC San Diego from patients with Parkinson's disease and healthy controls. Patients were recorded in two sessions, on and off dopaminergic medication, while controls completed a single session. The dataset includes participant demographics and UPDRS and MMSE clinical measures, and is curated in BIDS format for studying oscillatory and waveform characteristics of Parkinson's disease.
datasets.authors: Alexander P. Rockhill, Nicko Jackson, Jobi George, Adam Aron, Nicole C. Swann

datasets.name: Visual Oddball Task (256 channels)
datasets.description: High-density (256-channel) EEG recordings from a visual oddball selective attention task collected in 2004 at the Swartz Center for Computational Neuroscience, UCSD. The dataset extends an earlier 32-channel corpus using the same experimental paradigm, and adds scanned electrode positions and anatomical MRI to allow precise source localization. Events are annotated with HED tags.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: CRYPTO and PROVIDE EEG Baseline Data
datasets.description: Baseline EEG recordings from Bangladeshi children collected as part of the CRYPTO and PROVIDE studies. The dataset includes a cohort of 36-month-old toddlers and a cohort of 6-month-old infants who watched screen savers for 2 minutes. It was used to examine the association between stunting and EEG-derived brain functional connectivity in children exposed to early adversity.
datasets.authors: Wanze Xie, Sarah Jensen, Mark Wade, Swapna Kumar, Alissa Westerlund, Shahria Kakon, Rashidul Haque, William A Petri, Charles A Nelson

datasets.name: THINGS-EEG2: A large and rich EEG dataset for modeling human visual object recognition
datasets.description: THINGS-EEG2 is an EEG dataset from 10 participants who viewed 16,540 training images and 200 repeated test images from the THINGS database, using rapid serial visual presentation at 5 Hz. Each participant completed four sessions, recorded with a 63-channel BrainVision actiCHamp system at 1000 Hz, plus resting-state recordings. The dataset supports modeling of human visual object recognition and encoding models of neural responses.
datasets.authors: Alessandro T. Gifford, Kshitij Dwivedi, Gemma Roig, Radoslaw M. Cichy

datasets.name: Motor Imagery ataset from Ofner et al 2017
datasets.description: EEG recordings from fifteen healthy participants who executed and imagined six sustained upper limb movements (elbow flexion/extension, forearm supination/pronation, hand open/close) plus a rest condition, in two separate sessions. The dataset supports decoding of single upper limb movements from the time-domain of low-frequency EEG. It is relevant to non-invasive control of motor neuroprostheses and robotic arms. This BIDS version was generated from the original BNCI Horizon 2020 data using MOABB.
datasets.authors: Patrick Ofner, Andreas Schwarz, Joana Pereira, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: High-gamma dataset described in Schirrmeister et al. 2017
datasets.description: The High-gamma dataset contains 128-channel EEG recordings from 14 healthy participants performing cue-based executed movements of the left hand, right hand and feet, plus rest. It was introduced to evaluate end-to-end decoding with deep convolutional neural networks against filter bank common spatial patterns (FBCSP), and to visualize the spectral power modulations these networks learn. This version is a BIDS-formatted derivative generated with MOABB.
datasets.authors: Robin Tibor Schirrmeister, Jost Tobias Springenberg, Lukas Dominique Josef Fiederer, Martin Glasstetter, Katharina Eggensperger, Michael Tangermann, Frank Hutter, Wolfram Burgard, Tonio Ball

datasets.name: BNCI 2014-002 Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: Electroencephalographic recordings from 14 healthy participants performing a cue-guided, two-class motor imagery task (right hand versus feet) in a Graz-BCI paradigm with continuous visual feedback. Each participant completed a single session of 8 runs and 160 trials, recorded with 15 EEG channels at 512 Hz. The dataset was used to compare random forest and regularized LDA classifiers for sensorimotor rhythm brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: David Steyrl, Reinhold Scherer, Oswin Förstner, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: BNCI 2025-002 Continuous 2D Trajectory Decoding dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 able-bodied participants, plus a feasibility recording from one participant with spinal cord injury, performing attempted lower-arm movements to control a continuous 2D cursor trajectory. Each of the able-bodied participants completed three sessions comprising offline calibration and online feedback with 50% and 100% EEG control. The dataset supports regression-based trajectory decoding, learning effects across sessions, and source-localization analyses for brain-computer interface research.
datasets.authors: Hannah S Pulferer, Brynja Ásgeirsdóttir, Valeria Mondini, Andreea I Sburlea, Gernot R Müller-Putz

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study N — 9x8 dry/wet electrode comparison (8 ALS subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset is a subset (Study N) of the bigP3BCI collection, comprising 16-channel EEG recordings from 8 participants with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) using a P300-based speller with a 9x8 character grid. Each participant completed two sessions comparing dry and wet electrode setups. Target and non-target visual stimulus events are annotated with HED tags, and the data were recorded at 256 Hz with g.USBamp amplifiers.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study E — 6x6 checkerboard (8 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants in Study E of the bigP3BCI collection, which uses a 6x6 checkerboard P300 speller paradigm. Data were recorded with 16 EEG channels at 256 Hz using a g.USBamp amplifier, with Target and NonTarget visual stimulus events annotated using HED. It is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI resource, intended for P300 brain-computer interface research and benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study K — 9x8 adaptive/checkerboard, 2 sessions (5 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset is Study K of the bigP3BCI collection, a P300-based brain-computer interface speller dataset. It contains 16-channel EEG recorded from 5 healthy participants across 2 sessions, using a 9x8 character grid with adaptive and checkerboard stimulus paradigms. Target and non-target events are annotated with HED tags. The data are a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, prepared with MOABB.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: BNCI 2014-008 P300 dataset (ALS patients)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from eight people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) performing a visual P300 speller task with a 6x6 matrix. Participants copy-spelled seven predefined five-character words using row-column intensification while 8-channel EEG was recorded at 256 Hz. The dataset supports study of how attention and working memory relate to P300-based brain-computer interface performance in a clinical population.
datasets.authors: Angela Riccio, Luca Simione, Francesca Schettini, Alessia Pizzimenti, Maurizio Inghilleri, Marta Olivetti Belardinelli, Donatella Mattia, Febo Cincotti

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-013 Error-Related Potentials dataset
datasets.description: EEG dataset of error-related potentials (ErrPs) recorded from six participants while they monitored a cursor moving autonomously toward a target, with 20% or 40% error probability. Participants had no control over the cursor, showing that error correlates can be observed and decoded when monitoring an external agent. Recordings were made with 64 channels at 512 Hz across 20 sessions per subject, and the data support single-trial error detection for brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Ricardo Chavarriaga, José del R. Millán

datasets.name: Motor imagery dataset from Ma et al. 2020
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 healthy, BCI-naive right-handed participants performing motor imagery of two joints of the same limb (right hand and right elbow). Each participant completed 15 sessions over 3 days, giving 600 trials with 62-channel EEG sampled at 1000 Hz plus EOG. The dataset supports research on decoding fine-grained motor imagery within the same limb for motor rehabilitation and prosthetic control BCIs.
datasets.authors: Xuelin Ma, Shuang Qiu, Changde Du, Junfeng Xing, Huiguang He

datasets.name: c-VEP and Burst-VEP dataset from Castillos et al. (2023)
datasets.description: EEG dataset from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface task. The study compares novel burst c-VEP sequences with traditional m-sequences at two stimulus amplitude depths (100% and 40%). The aim is to optimize classification accuracy, minimize calibration data, and improve user experience. Data were recorded with a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz.
datasets.authors: Kalou Cabrera Castillos, Simon Ladouce, Ludovic Darmet, Frédéric Dehais

datasets.name: BNCI 2025-001 Motor Kinematics Reaching dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants performing a four-direction center-out discrete reaching task. Movements varied in speed (slow/fast) and distance (near/far), giving 16 conditions across 960 trials per participant. Recordings were made with 67 channels (including EOG) and preprocessed with eye artifact correction and ICA. The dataset supports study of low-frequency EEG encoding of movement kinematics and source localization for brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Nitikorn Srisrisawang, Gernot R Müller-Putz

datasets.name: BNCI 2024-001 Handwritten Character Classification dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants who wrote ten letters (a, d, e, f, j, n, o, s, t, v) with the right index finger after a visual cue. The dataset supports classification of handwritten characters, either directly from low-frequency and broadband EEG or with a two-step approach that first decodes continuous hand kinematics and then classifies the letter. It is intended for research on non-invasive brain-computer interfaces for communication.
datasets.authors: Markus R. Crell, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: Multi-joint upper-limb MI dataset from Yi et al. 2025
datasets.description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recordings from 18 healthy, right-handed participants performing motor imagery of eight multi-joint movements of the unilateral upper limb. The movements involve the hand, wrist, elbow and shoulder. Each participant completed 320 cue-based trials across 8 blocks, with 40 trials per class. The data support research on brain-computer interfaces for motor rehabilitation.
datasets.authors: Weibo Yi, Jiaming Chen, Dan Wang, Xinkang Hu, Meng Xu, Fangda Li, Shuhan Wu, Jin Qian

datasets.name: Liu, Lv et al. 2023 — EEG datasets of stroke patients (motor imagery)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 50 acute stroke patients (1-30 days post-stroke) performing video-guided left- and right-hand grip motor imagery. Data were acquired with a wireless semi-dry 29-channel EEG system, with 40 trials per subject. The dataset is intended for brain-computer interface algorithm development and stroke rehabilitation research, and is provided in a BIDS-formatted derivative with HED event annotations. Notice: the released recordings of subjects 5, 15 and 49 appear to be near-duplicates of subjects 4, 11 and 47, respectively. This is an open question pending clarification from the dataset authors, and these subjects should be excluded from cross-subject analyses until it is resolved.
datasets.authors: Haijie Liu, Penghu Wei, Haochong Wang, Xiaodong Lv, Wei Duan, Meijie Li, Yan Zhao, Qingmei Wang, Xinyuan Chen, Gaige Shi, Bo Han, Junwei Hao

datasets.name: Hybrid EEG-fNIRS MI dataset for ICH from Shi et al 2025
datasets.description: A hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset for brain-computer interface research in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). It includes 37 participants (17 healthy, 20 ICH patients) performing two-class left/right hand grasping motor imagery across up to several sessions. The data are pre-epoched, and the dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking BCI approaches for stroke rehabilitation.
datasets.authors: Jian Shi, Danyang Chen, Xingwei Zhao, Zhixian Zhao, Shengjie Li, Yeguang Xu, Tao Ding, Zheng Zhu, Peng Zhang, Qing Ye, Yingxin Tang, Ping Zhang, Bo Tao, Zhouping Tang

datasets.name: Upper-limb elbow-centered motor imagery dataset (10 classes)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing kinesthetic motor imagery of upper-limb, elbow-centered tasks. The paradigm has 10 classes: rest, elbow flexion, and eight goal-directed daily-living tasks such as drawer opening, soup eating, weight lifting and combing. Data were recorded with a 17-channel EGI system at 1000 Hz. The dataset supports research on the versatility of EEG models for motor-imagery BCI control and rehabilitation.
datasets.authors: Xin Zhang, Xinyi Yong, Carlo Menon

datasets.name: M3CV: Multi-subject, Multi-session, Multi-task EEG Database
datasets.description: M3CV is a multi-subject, multi-session, multi-task EEG database with 64-channel recordings from 95 healthy young adults. Each subject was recorded on two different days across six paradigms covering 13 distributed signal types: resting states, motor execution, transient visual, auditory and somatosensory responses, SSVEP, P300, SSAEP and SSSEP. The data were originally released for an EEG-based biometrics competition on Kaggle. This BIDS version reconstructs pseudo-continuous EEG from the distributed pre-epoched, preprocessed 250 Hz files.
datasets.authors: Gan Huang, Zhenxing Hu, Weize Chen, Shaorong Zhang, Zhen Liang, Linling Li, Li Zhang, Zhiguo Zhang
datasets.eeg_reference: TP9/TP10 (linked mastoids, applied offline during preprocessing)

datasets.name: Chen2017 – Single-flicker online SSVEP BCI dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recorded with a BioSemi ActiveTwo system from 12 healthy participants using a single-flicker, spatially coded SSVEP brain-computer interface for spatial navigation. A single 15 Hz flickering square is shown at the screen center, and four non-flickering targets lie at the cardinal directions. Gaze direction produces distinct spatial topographies of the SSVEP response. Two sessions per subject are included: a structured training calibration session and an online adaptive BCI game session.
datasets.authors: Jingjing Chen, Dan Zhang, Andreas K. Engel, Qin Gong, Alexander Maye

datasets.name: EEG meditation study
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 24 participants performing a meditation task. Participants were interrupted approximately every two minutes to rate their level of concentration and mind wandering. The dataset supports research on meditation, attention, and mind wandering.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme, Tracy Brandmeyer

datasets.name: Auditory Gamma Entrainment
datasets.description: EEG recordings from elderly participants with dementia during auditory gamma entrainment. The stimulus was a 5 kHz carrier tone amplitude-modulated with a 40 Hz pulse train, presented in alternating stimulation and silence blocks. The dataset also includes a one-minute eyes-open resting-state recording. It is intended for investigating how 40 Hz auditory stimulation affects brain oscillations in Alzheimer's disease and related dementia.
datasets.authors: Mojtaba Lahijanian, Mohammad Javad Sedghizadeh, Hamid Aghajan, Zahra Vahabi

datasets.name: Zhang-2025-cerebrovoice: CerebroVoice: A Stereotactic EEG Dataset and Benchmark for Bilingual Brain-to-Speech Synthesis and Activity Detection
datasets.description: CerebroVoice is a stereotactic EEG (sEEG) dataset recorded from two epilepsy patients during bilingual speech tasks, including Mandarin Chinese reading, English reading, and digit reading. It is distributed as preprocessed derivatives: low-frequency signal, high-gamma activity, and broadband signal. The dataset supports benchmarking of bilingual brain-to-speech synthesis and speech activity detection.
datasets.authors: Xueyi Zhang

datasets.name: BigP3BCI Study F — 6x6 multi-paradigm, 3 sessions (10 healthy subjects)
datasets.description: This dataset is Study F of the bigP3BCI collection, a P300-based brain-computer interface speller dataset. It contains 16-channel EEG recorded at 256 Hz over three sessions per subject from 10 participants using a 6x6 character grid with multiple stimulus paradigms. Target and non-target events are annotated with HED tags. The data is a BIDS-formatted derivative of the PhysioNet bigP3BCI release, prepared through MOABB.
datasets.authors: Boyla Mainsah, Chance Fleeting, Thomas Balmat, Eric Sellers, Leslie Collins

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-012 PASS2D P300 dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants using PASS2D, a nine-class auditory ERP (P300/N200) speller. Users attended to two-dimensional auditory stimuli varying in pitch and direction, presented via headphones, to drive a predictive text entry system. The session contained a calibration phase and an online spelling phase. The data were recorded with 63 EEG channels and are provided as a preprocessed BIDS derivative.
datasets.authors: Johannes Höhne, Martijn Schreuder, Benjamin Blankertz, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-003 P300 dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants using an auditory P300 brain-computer interface speller based on the AMUSE (Auditory Multi-class Spatial ERP) paradigm. Six speakers placed around the participant provided spatial auditory cues for a two-step, hex-o-spell-like character selection. The recordings include calibration and online spelling in two sessions, the second using a dynamic stopping method to increase writing speed.
datasets.authors: Martijn Schreuder, Thomas Rost, Michael Tangermann

datasets.name: BNCI 2014-009 P300 dataset
datasets.description: A P300 brain-computer interface EEG dataset from 10 healthy, BCI-experienced female participants who selected one of 36 characters using two visual spelling interfaces: the P300 Speller (overt attention) and GeoSpell (covert attention). EEG was recorded from 16 scalp electrodes across multiple sessions. The dataset supports analysis of P300 latency jitter and its relationship to BCI classification performance.
datasets.authors: P Aricò, F Aloise, F Schettini, S Salinari, D Mattia, F Cincotti

datasets.name: Liu2020 – BETA SSVEP benchmark dataset
datasets.description: The BETA database contains 64-channel EEG recordings from 70 healthy participants (aged 9-64 years) performing a 40-target cued-spelling SSVEP-BCI task. Stimuli used joint frequency and phase modulation (JFPM) on a 5x8 virtual keyboard, with frequencies of 8-15.8 Hz. Data were recorded in a normal classroom rather than a shielded room, giving a more realistic benchmark for SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Bingchuan Liu, Xiaoshan Huang, Yijun Wang, Xiaogang Chen, Xiaorong Gao

datasets.name: Dong2023 – 59-subject 40-class SSVEP dataset
datasets.description: An 8-channel EEG dataset from 59 healthy adolescents (aged 10-16) who performed a 40-target SSVEP-based brain-computer interface task. The task used joint frequency and phase modulation (JFPM) with stimulation frequencies of 8.0-15.8 Hz. Data were collected at the Suzhou Junior Competition of BCI Olympics 2022 and are provided as epoched trials, 4 blocks of 40 trials per subject. The dataset supports benchmarking of SSVEP classification and spatial-filtering methods.
datasets.authors: Yue Dong, Sen Tian

datasets.name: Kim2025 – 40-class beta-range SSVEP speller dataset
datasets.description: A 40-class SSVEP speller EEG dataset recorded from 40 healthy participants using beta-range flicker frequencies (14.0-21.8 Hz, 0.2 Hz spacing). Stimuli were presented with the joint frequency-phase modulation (JFPM) approach in a 5x8 matrix on a 120 Hz monitor. Each participant completed six blocks of 40 trials with 33-channel BioSemi recordings at 1024 Hz. The dataset is intended for developing low-visual-fatigue SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Heegyu Kim, Kyungho Won, Minkyu Ahn, Sung Chan Jun

datasets.name: Wang2016 – SSVEP Wang 2016 dataset
datasets.description: A benchmark SSVEP-based brain-computer interface dataset containing 64-channel EEG from 34 healthy participants (35 in the original publication) who gazed at 40 flickering characters in a speller. The targets were coded with joint frequency and phase modulation (8-15.8 Hz, 0.2 Hz steps). Each subject completed 6 blocks of 40 cued trials, 5 s of stimulation per trial. Epochs were extracted around stimulus onset and downsampled to 250 Hz.
datasets.authors: Yijun Wang, Xiaogang Chen, Xiaorong Gao, Shangkai Gao

datasets.name: Lee2021 – SSVEP paradigm of the Mobile BCI dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains the steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) paradigm from the Mobile BCI dataset of scalp- and ear-EEG. Participants viewed visual flickers at three frequencies (5.45, 8.57, and 12 Hz) while standing, walking, and running on a treadmill. It supports research on brain-computer interfaces that remain robust during locomotion. The recordings are provided in BIDS format with HED event annotations, derived via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Young-Eun Lee, Gi-Hwan Shin, Minji Lee, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: Han2024 – SSVEP fatigue dataset with two frequency paradigms
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing two SSVEP-based brain-computer interface tasks, a low-frequency paradigm (8.0-15.5 Hz) and a high-frequency paradigm (25.5-33.0 Hz). Each paradigm has 16 targets encoded with joint frequency-phase modulation. Training and fatigue blocks were recorded to study how fatigue affects SSVEP-BCI performance and to evaluate dynamic stopping strategies.
datasets.authors: Yuheng Han, Yufeng Ke, Ruiyan Wang, Tao Wang, Dong Ming

datasets.name: Kalunga2016 – SSVEP Exo dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing a steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) task in an assistive robotics setting. Participants seated in an electric wheelchair focused on LEDs flickering at 13, 17 or 21 Hz, or on a fixation point for a reject (rest) class. Eight channels were recorded at 256 Hz. The data support online, asynchronous SSVEP-based brain-computer interface research using Riemannian geometry.
datasets.authors: Emmanuel K. Kalunga, Sylvain Chevallier, Quentin Barthélemy, Karim Djouani, Eric Monacelli, Yskandar Hamam

datasets.name: Oikonomou2016 – SSVEP MAMEM 3 dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains 14-channel Emotiv EPOC EEG recordings from healthy, BCI-naive participants performing a steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) task. Five violet boxes flickered simultaneously at 6.66, 7.50, 8.57, 10.00 and 12.00 Hz while participants focused on a cued target. The recordings come from the MAMEM SSVEP III collection and were used in a comparative evaluation of filtering, artifact removal, feature extraction and classification algorithms for SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Vangelis P. Oikonomou, Georgios Liaros, Kostantinos Georgiadis, Elisavet Chatzilari, Katerina Adam, Spiros Nikolopoulos, Ioannis Kompatsiaris

datasets.name: Oikonomou2016 – SSVEP MAMEM 2 dataset
datasets.description: A 256-channel EEG dataset recorded from 11 healthy participants performing an SSVEP-based brain-computer interface protocol. Participants focused on one of five simultaneously flickering boxes (6.66, 7.50, 8.57, 10.00 and 12.00 Hz) while EEG was recorded at 250 Hz with an EGI GES 300 system. The dataset supports comparative evaluation of filtering, artifact removal, feature extraction and classification algorithms for SSVEP-based BCIs.
datasets.authors: Vangelis P. Oikonomou, Georgios Liaros, Kostantinos Georgiadis, Elisavet Chatzilari, Katerina Adam, Spiros Nikolopoulos, Ioannis Kompatsiaris

datasets.name: Oikonomou2016 – SSVEP MAMEM 1 dataset
datasets.description: A 256-channel EEG dataset of steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) recorded from 11 healthy adults. Participants viewed a single flickering box at five stimulation frequencies (6.66, 7.50, 8.57, 10.00 and 12.00 Hz) while EEG was recorded at 250 Hz with an EGI 300 Geodesic EEG System. The dataset supports comparative evaluation of SSVEP-based brain-computer interface algorithms, including leave-one-subject-out classification.
datasets.authors: Vangelis P. Oikonomou, Georgios Liaros, Kostantinos Georgiadis, Elisavet Chatzilari, Katerina Adam, Spiros Nikolopoulos, Ioannis Kompatsiaris

datasets.name: Nakanishi2015 – SSVEP Nakanishi 2015 dataset
datasets.description: A 12-class steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) EEG dataset using joint frequency-phase modulation, recorded from healthy participants in a simulated online brain-computer interface experiment. Eight occipital and parieto-occipital channels were recorded at 256 Hz while subjects gazed at flickering targets on a 4x3 virtual keypad (9.25-14.75 Hz). The data were originally used to compare canonical correlation analysis (CCA)-based SSVEP detection methods.
datasets.authors: Masaki Nakanishi, Yijun Wang, Yu-Te Wang, Tzyy-Ping Jung

datasets.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset
datasets.description: A collection of over 1500 one- and two-minute 64-channel EEG recordings from 109 volunteers performing motor execution and motor imagery tasks. Participants completed baseline runs (eyes open and eyes closed) and runs in which they opened and closed, or imagined opening and closing, the left or right fist or both fists or both feet in response to on-screen targets. The data were recorded with the BCI2000 system and are suited to brain-computer interface research.
datasets.authors: Gerwin Schalk, Dennis J McFarland, Thilo Hinterberger, Niels Birbaumer, Jonathan R Wolpaw

datasets.name: SparrKULee: A Speech-Evoked Auditory Response Repository from KU Leuven, Containing the EEG of 85 Participants
datasets.description: SparrKULee is a speech-evoked auditory response repository from KU Leuven containing EEG recorded from normal-hearing native Dutch/Flemish speakers listening to continuous speech stimuli. This NEMAR re-host contains 80 of the original 85 participants across 11 session types (shortstories01 and varyingStories01-10), plus resting-state recordings. It supports research on neural tracking of speech and auditory EEG modelling.
datasets.authors: Bernd Accou, Lies Bollens, Marlies Gillis, Wendy Verheijen, Hugo Van hamme, Tom Francart
datasets.license: Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC 4.0) for the EEG data. Stimuli can only be used for non-commercial purposes.

datasets.name: Munich Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: A 128-channel EEG dataset from 10 healthy participants performing two-class (left hand vs. right hand) motor imagery, cued by visual arrows. Each participant completed one session of 150 trials per class. Data were recorded at 500 Hz with a BrainAmp system in a shielded room and re-referenced to common average offline. The dataset was originally collected to evaluate beamforming and spatial filtering approaches for noninvasive brain-computer interfaces. It was converted to BIDS using MOABB (Mother of All BCI Benchmarks) 1.5.0.
datasets.authors: Moritz Grosse-Wentrup, Christian Liefhold, Klaus Gramann, Martin Buss

datasets.name: Motor Imagery dataset from Weibo et al 2014
datasets.description: A 60-channel EEG dataset from 10 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing simple limb motor imagery (left hand, right hand, feet) and compound limb motor imagery (both hands, left hand with right foot, right hand with left foot), plus a rest condition. The recordings were used to examine EEG oscillatory patterns (ERD/ERS), cognitive processes, and effective connectivity during motor imagery. This is a preprocessed (bandpass filtered, downsampled to 200 Hz) BIDS version curated through MOABB.
datasets.authors: Weibo Yi, Shuang Qiu, Kun Wang, Hongzhi Qi, Lixin Zhang, Peng Zhou, Feng He, Dong Ming

datasets.name: Motor imagery BCI dataset with pupillometry augmentation
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 30 healthy participants performing a left-hand grasping motor imagery task versus rest, collected with simultaneous pupillometry. Data were acquired with a 32-channel BioSemi ActiveTwo system at 512 Hz, with 50 auditory-cued trials per participant across two runs. This BIDS derivative was regenerated with a corrected MOABB loader that fixes channel labelling and signal scaling. The dataset supports evaluation of whether task-evoked pupil diameter changes improve EEG-based motor imagery BCI classification.
datasets.authors: David Rozado, Andreas Duenser, Ben Howell

datasets.name: BNCI 2019-001 Motor Imagery dataset for Spinal Cord Injury patients
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 10 persons with cervical spinal cord injury performing attempted arm and hand movements: hand open, palmar grasp, lateral grasp, pronation and supination. Sixty-one EEG channels and 3 EOG channels were recorded across 9 runs per participant. Low-frequency time-domain EEG (movement-related cortical potentials) was used to decode the five movement classes offline, and an online proof-of-concept for self-paced movement detection was also run. The dataset supports research on neuroprosthetic and upper-limb control brain-computer interfaces.
datasets.authors: Patrick Ofner, Andreas Schwarz, Joana Pereira, Daniela Wyss, Renate Wildburger, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: Liu2022 – eldBETA SSVEP benchmark dataset for elderly population
datasets.description: The eldBETA dataset provides 64-channel EEG recordings from 100 elderly participants (aged 51-81) performing a 9-target SSVEP-based brain-computer interface speller task. Stimuli used joint frequency and phase modulation (JFPM) at 8-12 Hz in 0.5 Hz steps, with 7 blocks of 9 trials per participant. It serves as a benchmark for evaluating SSVEP-BCI decoding algorithms in an aging population.
datasets.authors: Bingchuan Liu, Yijun Wang, Xiaorong Gao, Xiaogang Chen

datasets.name: Wang2021 – Combined SSVEP dataset with single stimulus location for two inputs
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing a combined steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface task. Spatially overlapping arrow stimuli at a single location, flickering at distinct frequencies derived from an 85 Hz CRT refresh rate, encode four directions (up, down, left, right). Participants covertly attended to one direction per trial, and the data cover three stimulation and attention schemes across two experiments.
datasets.authors: Lu Wang, Zhenhao Zhang, Dan Han, Zhijun Zhang, Zhifang Liu, Wei Liu

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-004 Mental tasks dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from nine end-users with central nervous system tissue damage (stroke or spinal cord injury) performing five cue-guided mental tasks: word association, mental subtraction, spatial navigation, right-hand motor imagery, and feet motor imagery. Data were recorded with 30 active EEG electrodes across two sessions per participant, on different days. The dataset supports brain-computer interface research on individually adapted imagery and binary classification of mental tasks.
datasets.authors: Reinhold Scherer, Josef Faller, Elisabeth V. C. Friedrich, Eloy Opisso, Ursula Costa, Andrea Kübler, Gernot R. Müller-Putz

datasets.name: BNCI2003_IVa Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from five healthy participants performing cued motor imagery (right hand versus foot) with 118 electrodes, originally published to demonstrate improved single-trial classification through feature combination and multiclass paradigms. The data were downsampled to 100 Hz and comprise 280 cued trials per subject, split into labeled training and unlabeled test sets. The dataset was part of BCI Competition III and is widely used for benchmarking BCI classification algorithms.
datasets.authors: Guido Dornhege, Benjamin Blankertz, Gabriel Curio, Klaus-Robert Müller

datasets.name: Ear-EEG motor execution dataset from Wu et al 2020
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous scalp and ear-EEG recordings from six healthy right-handed participants performing cued left- and right-hand fist clenching (motor execution). It comprises 1114 trials recorded with a Neuroscan SynAmps2 system at 1000 Hz. The dataset was designed to investigate in-ear sensing for motor task classification and for brain-computer interface benchmarking. It has been reformatted into BIDS with HED annotations via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Xiaoli Wu, Wenhui Zhang, Zhibo Fu, Roy T.H. Cheung, Rosa H.M. Chan

datasets.name: Motor execution dataset from Wairagkar et al 2018
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 14 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing asynchronous voluntary index-finger tapping (right, left) and rest, originally reported by Wairagkar et al. (2018). Data were recorded at 1024 Hz from 19 scalp channels and preprocessed with filtering and ICA artifact removal. Trials are segmented around movement onset to study neural correlates of movement intention, and the dataset is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Maitreyee Wairagkar, Yoshikatsu Hayashi, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: BNCI 2015-001 Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing two-class motor imagery (sustained right-hand palmar grip versus both-feet plantar extension) across two sessions, with 200 trials per session. Data were recorded from 13 sensorimotor channels at 512 Hz with visual cursor feedback, in support of an autocalibrating, recurrently adapting online ERD-based brain-computer interface. The dataset is distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
datasets.authors: Josef Faller, Carmen Vidaurre, Teodoro Solis-Escalante, Christa Neuper, Reinhold Scherer

datasets.name: BNCI 2014-001 Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 9 healthy subjects performing cued motor imagery of left hand, right hand, feet, and tongue movements, known as BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a. Each subject completed two sessions of six runs, with 22 EEG and 3 EOG channels sampled at 250 Hz. It is widely used as a benchmark for multi-class motor imagery classification in brain-computer interface research.
datasets.authors: Michael Tangermann, Klaus-Robert Müller, Ad Aertsen, Niels Birbaumer, Christoph Braun, Clemens Brunner, Robert Leeb, Carsten Mehring, Kai J. Miller, Gernot R. Müller-Putz, Guido Nolte, Gert Pfurtscheller, Hubert Preissl, Gerwin Schalk, Alois Schlögl, Carmen Vidaurre, Stephan Waldert, Benjamin Blankertz

datasets.name: Alex Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing cue-based motor imagery of the right hand, feet, and rest, with 20 trials per class. The data were collected for the PhD thesis of A. Barachant on robust control of an effector through an asynchronous EEG brain-machine interface, and correspond to Step B (cue-based imagery without feedback) of the Brain Switch campaign. They are intended for familiarization and algorithm development, including Riemannian geometry and CSP-based classification.
datasets.authors: Alexandre Barachant

datasets.name: Classical motor imagery dataset with left hand, right hand, and rest
datasets.description: This dataset contains 19-channel EEG recordings from 7 healthy participants performing classical motor imagery of the left hand, right hand, and passive rest. Participants responded to visual arrow cues in offline sessions, without feedback. The recordings were made with a Nihon Kohden EEG-1200 system at 200 Hz. The data support brain-computer interface research and motor imagery classification benchmarking.
datasets.authors: Murat Kaya, Mustafa Kemal Binli, Erkan Ozbay, Hilmi Yanar, Yuriy Mishchenko

datasets.name: Guttmann-Flury et al. 2025 (P300) — Dataset combining EEG, eye-tracking, and high-speed video for ocular activity analysis across BCI paradigms
datasets.description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz from 31 healthy participants performing a row/column P300 speller task with 4L and 5L grid sizes. Each participant completed three sessions. It is the P300 component of a multimodal eye-BCI collection that also includes eye-tracking and high-speed video for analyzing ocular activity across BCI paradigms. Events are annotated with HED tags as Target and NonTarget flashes.
datasets.authors: Eva Guttmann-Flury, Xinjun Sheng, Xiangyang Zhu

datasets.name: BNCI 2014-004 Motor Imagery dataset
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 9 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing two-class motor imagery (left vs. right hand), known as BCI Competition IV Dataset 2b (Graz data set B). Each participant completed five sessions: two screening sessions without feedback and three sessions with smiley feedback. Three bipolar EEG channels (C3, Cz, C4) were recorded at 250 Hz. This deposit is a MOABB-derived BIDS conversion of the original data.
datasets.authors: R. Leeb, C. Brunner, G. R. Müller-Putz, A. Schlögl, G. Pfurtscheller, F. Lee, C. Keinrath, R. Scherer, H. Bischof

datasets.name: Motor imagery dataset for three imaginary states of the same upper extremity
datasets.description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing three-class motor imagery of the same (right) upper extremity: rest, imagined hand grasping, and imagined elbow flexion. Each participant completed 4 sessions of 60 trials (20 per class), recorded with an EGI Geodesic Net Amps system at 1000 Hz. The data support brain-computer interface research on decoding closely related movements of a single limb, for example in rehabilitation and motor control.
datasets.authors: Mojgan Tavakolan, Zack Frehlick, Xinyi Yong, Carlo Menon

datasets.name: Multimodal upper-limb MI/ME EEG (Jeong et al. 2020)
datasets.description: A multimodal EEG, EOG and EMG dataset from 25 healthy, BCI-naive right-handed participants performing motor imagery and real movement of 11 intuitive upper-limb tasks. The tasks were 6 reaching directions, 3 grasping types and 2 wrist-twisting movements. Each participant completed 3 sessions of 550 trials. Recordings used 60 EEG channels at 1000 Hz. This BIDS derivative was generated via MOABB and is intended for BCI research on motor control and prosthetics.
datasets.authors: Ji-Hoon Jeong, Jeong-Hyun Cho, Kyung-Hwan Shim, Byoung-Hee Kwon, Byeong-Hoo Lee, Do-Yeun Lee, Dae-Hyeok Lee, Seong-Whan Lee

datasets.name: Alljoined-1.6M
datasets.description: Alljoined-1.6M is a large-scale EEG dataset of neural responses to rapid serial visual presentation of natural images from the THINGS database. It was recorded with a consumer-grade 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system in 20 adult participants over four sessions each, yielding more than 1.6 million trials. The dataset was built to test whether deep-learning-based brain-computer interface and semantic decoding research can be done with affordable EEG hardware.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Xu, Ugo Bruzadin Nunes, Wangshu Jiang, Samuel Ryther, Jordan Pringle, Paul S. Scotti, Arnaud Delorme, Reese Kneeland

datasets.name: Alljoined1
datasets.description: Alljoined1 is an EEG dataset of neural responses to natural images presented in a rapid serial visual presentation paradigm, built for EEG-to-image decoding research. Eight healthy adults viewed images from the Natural Scenes Dataset (MS-COCO) while 64-channel BioSemi EEG was recorded across one or two sessions. This BIDS version contains raw BDF recordings of 960 shared images, event tables linked to stimuli, and epoched derivatives from the original authors.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Xu, Si Kai Lee, Wangshu Jiang, Bruno Aristimunha, Max Emanuel Feucht, Emma Qian, Charles Liu, Tazik Shahjahan, Martyna Spyra, Steven Zifan Zhang, Nicholas Short, Jioh Kim, Paula Perdomo, Ricky Renfeng Mao, Yashvir Sabharwal, Michael Ahedor, Moaz Shoura, Adrian Nestor

datasets.name: MDD Patients and Healthy Controls EEG Data
datasets.description: Resting-state (eyes-closed and eyes-open) and auditory oddball P300 task EEG recordings from patients with Major Depressive Disorder and healthy control participants. Data were recorded with a 19-channel 10-20 system at 256 Hz to support research on neurophysiological biomarkers of depression and on differences in attentional processing. This BIDS version was converted from the original figshare deposit.
datasets.authors: Wajid Mumtaz, Likun Xia, Syed Saad Azhar Ali, Mohd Azhar Mohd Yasin, Mazhar Hussain, Aamir Saeed Malik

datasets.name: 2020 BCI competition, track 3
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 15 participants performing imagined speech of five commands ("Hello", "Help me", "Stop", "Thank you", "Yes"), released for the 2020 BCI Competition Track 3. The data are split into training, validation and test runs to support machine-learning decoding of imagined speech for brain-computer interfaces. The dataset was converted from the original MATLAB files to BIDS-compliant EDF with trial annotations.
datasets.authors: Seong-Whan Lee, Klaus-Robert Müller, José del R. Millán

datasets.name: EEG During Mental Arithmetic Tasks
datasets.description: Scalp EEG recordings from 36 healthy university students during eyes-closed rest and a serial-subtraction mental arithmetic task. The dataset supports study of EEG correlates of cognitive workload and mathematical cognition, with applications in mental workload assessment and brain-computer interfaces. Participants were split post hoc into good and bad counters based on the number of completed subtractions. This BIDS version was converted from the PhysioNet release.
datasets.authors: Igor Zyma, Sergii Tukaev, Ivan Seleznov, Ken Kiyono, Anton Popov, Mariia Chernykh, Oleksii Shpenkov

datasets.name: ERP CORE
datasets.description: ERP CORE (Compendium of Open Resources and Experiments) is an open resource of raw EEG recordings from 40 neurotypical adults performing six optimized task paradigms. The paradigms elicit seven widely used ERP components: N170, MMN, N2pc, N400, P3, LRP and ERN. The dataset includes event code schemes, task stimuli for the N170, MMN and N400 paradigms, and participant demographics.
datasets.authors: Emily S. Kappenman, Jaclyn L. Farrens, Wendy Zhang, Andrew X. Stewart, Steven J. Luck.

datasets.name: Human electroencephalography recordings from 50 subjects for 22,248 images from 1,854 object concepts
datasets.description: This dataset contains electroencephalography recordings from 50 participants viewing 22,248 images spanning 1,854 object concepts from the THINGS image database. Images were shown in rapid serial visual presentation streams at 10 Hz while participants performed an orthogonal fixation colour change detection task. The dataset supports research on the temporal dynamics of object recognition and visual representation in the human brain.
datasets.authors: Grootswagers, Tijl, Zhou, Ivy, Robinson, Amanda, Hebart, Martin, Carlson, Thomas

datasets.name: FACED - Finer-grained Affective Computing EEG Dataset
datasets.description: FACED is a scalp EEG dataset from 123 healthy participants who watched 28 emotion-eliciting video clips targeting nine emotion categories: four negative, four positive and one neutral. Participants gave self-reports on 12 dimensions, including discrete emotions, valence, arousal, liking and familiarity. The dataset supports cross-subject affective computing research and the development of EEG-based emotion recognition algorithms. This BIDS version includes event annotations linked to stimulus metadata.
datasets.authors: Yisi Liu, Olga Sourina, Minh Khoa Nguyen, Jingjing Chen, Xiaobin Wang, Chen Huang, Xin Hu, Xinke Shen, Dan Zhang

datasets.name: CHB-MIT
datasets.description: The CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database contains continuous scalp EEG recordings from pediatric patients with intractable epilepsy, collected at Children's Hospital Boston. Subjects were monitored for days after anti-seizure medication withdrawal to characterize seizures and assess candidacy for surgical intervention. The recordings include 198 annotated seizures, sampled at 256 Hz on the 10-20 system with bipolar montages. This version is a BIDS conversion of the original PhysioNet data, with seizure onset and offset annotations provided as events.
datasets.authors: Jack Connolly, Herman Edwards, Blaise Bourgeois, S. Ted Treves, Ali Shoeb, John Guttag

datasets.name: Face processing MEEG dataset with HED annotation
datasets.description: This dataset is the MEG, EEG and structural MRI portion of the multi-subject, multi-modal face processing dataset (ds000117), re-curated with Hierarchical Event Descriptor (HED) annotations. Eighteen participants viewed famous, unfamiliar, and scrambled faces and made symmetry judgments while MEG and EEG were recorded simultaneously. Events were augmented and reorganized, and the EEG data were converted to BioSemi Data Format. Structural MRI is retained to support source localization.
datasets.authors: Daniel G. Wakeman, Richard N Henson, Dung Truong (curation), Kay Robbins (curation), Scott Makeig (curation), Arno Delorme (curation), Seyed Yahya Shirazi (curation)
